question: how does the AuraFace->LDA identity instrument's R@1 degrade on REAL faces as image quality drops, and what is the quality-matched baseline for the arm's low-quality renders?

pool.holdout_purpose: identity-level holdout for the eidolon renderer arm: identities whose vectors are never fed in training, so the gate measures generalization rather than recall

instrument.det_size_note: None means insightface default 640x640 -- CORPUS BEHAVIOUR. A tuple reproduces the FFHQ path and is a different instrument.

index_B.note: index B is the clean re-embedding of the SAME pool by this instrument (det_size None). Because queries that returned no_face at sigma=0 are absent, index B is smaller than index A and its own-index positions are remapped; ranks are computed against the remapped pool.

notes: FINDING: the render's sharpness proxy (446.7) is ABOVE the clean-real mean (191.7), so NO blur level matches it. Variance of the Laplacian measures high-frequency ENERGY, which the renders' speckle/grain inflates; the renders are not merely blurred real faces, they are noise-dominated. The blur sweep therefore cannot supply the quality-matched baseline on its own; read the noise-family match for the render and the blur curve for the degradation trend.

conventions.auraface_input: (H,W,3) BGR uint8 -- pixel.npy is RGB (matches the VAE decode) and is reversed explicitly
conventions.det_size_note: None == insightface default 640x640, the CORPUS convention. NOTE: the FFHQ sidecars were produced by the FFHQ path with det_size=(512,512) (eidolon/scripts/pipeline/extract_ffhq_auraface.py), so index A carries a query/index convention mismatch that index B removes.
conventions.index_B: clean (sigma=0) re-embeddings of the same pool
conventions.sharpness: variance of the Laplacian of the uint8 grey image
conventions.no_face: outcome no_face -> lda_unit=null, excluded from R@1; never substituted
